summary: During a grapple-induced hero recoil, dothrow.c hurtle_step calls trap.c instapetrify when the hero bumps into a touch-petrifying monster without body armor. JS sets the killer string but records instapetrify as unported, so the C stoning message and death path do not run.

source.branch: In hurtle_step's monster-collision branch, after waking and angering the monster, C calls instapetrify when the monster touch-petrifies and the hero has no body armor.
callers: apply.c:use_grapple calls hurtle toward the selected floor square; hurtle reaches hurtle_step for each traversed square.
dothrow.c:hurtle and dothrow.c:jump also use hurtle_step through walk_path; dokick.c, uhitm.c, and timeout.c call hurtle for their own recoil paths.
dependencies: trap.c:instapetrify is already implemented in js/trap.js and is reserved by another task. This fix only calls the existing helper; it does not edit its implementation.

evidence: The admitted v64 recipe reaches the grappling-hook surface path after removing the hero's torso armor. The C recording has 420 of 423 screens and 3401 of 3401 RNG calls at evaluation commit 6533e0a; the worker replay first differs at boundary 384 after the grapple collision.

Read nethack-c/upstream/src/dothrow.c:773-972. In hurtle_step's collision branch, C sets the killer string and calls instapetrify after the body-armor guard. At examined commit da7ef8b, js/dothrow.js:1011-1017 set that string but call note_unported('trap.c instapetrify') instead.

Read nethack-c/upstream/src/trap.c:3844-3855 and js/trap.js:369-388. The existing instapetrify helper checks stone resistance, stone-golem polymorph, the stoning message, killer state, and final death handling, so the caller can wire it without editing the reserved callee.
